newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former French interim president Poher dies.
newsitem.headline: Former French interim president Poher dies.

text.p: PARIS, Dec 9, Reuter - France's former Senate speaker Alain Poher, who twice stood in for the president of the Republic, has died, a spokesman for the upper house said on Monday. He was 87.
Poher was twice acting president, first for two months when General Charles de Gaulle resigned in 1969 and then again when President Georges Pompidou died in 1974.
The veteran centrist, who was speaker of the Senate (upper house) for more than 20 years, retired from politics four years ago.
He was last elected speaker in 1989, a job that under the constitution made him the second highest-ranking figure in the country and the interim president in an emergency.
Poher made a bid for the top job while acting as interim president for 58 days after de Gaulle resigned. Pompidou defeated him in an election run-off.
